All 39 tests pass (78 in the run above because both categories contribute the same suite). Here is what the model looks like now.

## 1–2. Instance creation funnels

- `Floor class>>withRooms: aNumberOfRooms pricedWith: aPriceList` runs `assertIsValidNumberOfRooms:` / `assertIsValidPriceList:` and then the single `initializeWithRooms:pricedWith:` (assignments only). `setNumberOfRooms:`, `setPrices:` and the two old initializers are gone.
- `Hotel class>>withFloors: aFloorCollection` runs `assertHasFloors:` and delegates to `initializeWithFloors:`. `setFloors:` and the cached `availableRoomsCount` instance variable are gone — `totalRoomsAvailable` is now asked of the floors, so it can never get out of sync.

## 3–4. Room status as objects

`Room` holds a `status`, an immutable `RoomStatus`: `AvailableRoomStatus`, `ReservedRoomStatus`, `OccupiedRoomStatus` (which knows the guest type). No more `nil` guest and no `#reserved` symbol. Each transition answers the new status, so `Room>>receive:`, `#receiveWithReservation:` and `#reserve` are one line each (`status := status receive: aGuestType`). The guards are not repeated: `RoomStatus` signals *room is not empty* / *room is not reserved* by default and only the status that allows a change overrides it. `isAvailable`/`isOccupied`/`isReserved` and the profit/loss rules are polymorphic too — no conditionals left.

## 5–6. Floor encapsulation and losses

`Floor>>rooms` is deleted. `Floor` now understands `roomAt:`, `receive:atRoom:`, `receiveWithReservation:atRoom:` and `reserveRoom:`. `Room>>lossUsing:ifAbsentGuestType:` was added (available loses the most expensive price, reserved and occupied lose nothing), and `Floor>>totalLosses` sums it over every room, mirroring `totalProfits`; `Hotel>>totalLosses` sums the floors.

One consequence worth flagging: the *room number does not exist* error now belongs to `Floor`, since `Floor` does the lookup, so `HotelTest` tests 9, 11 and 13 assert `Floor roomNumberDoesNotExistErrorDescription`. The message text is unchanged. I also fixed `Floor class>>signalUnknownGuestType`, which sent `self class unknownGuestTypeErrorDescription` and would have raised a doesNotUnderstand instead of the intended error, and removed the dead "price must be integer" error.

## 7. Repeated code in Hotel

The three guest messages are now `(self floorAt: aFloorNumber) ...`; `floorAt:` is the only place the floor-number error lives. `isEmpty` is `floors allSatisfy: [ :aFloor | aFloor isAvailable ]` and the four totals plus both accounting messages are each a `floors sum: [...]` — the `whileTrue:` loops are gone.

## 8. Bonus: tests

`createFloorWith:and:` became `createFloorWithRooms:` (the price list defaults), `createHotel` uses `Hotel withFloors:`, the `"Tech Debt"` sends through `floor rooms` became sends to the floor, `HotelTest` tests 9–13 reuse `createHotel` instead of rebuilding floors inline, the exception blocks hold a single send, and the `100*peso`/`200*peso` literals in `FloorTest` are now `minPriceInList`/`maxPriceInList`. I left each test class with its own fixture helpers rather than introducing a shared test superclass, since that subclassing would share implementation rather than knowledge.

Test classes moved to `ISW1-2024-1C-Parcial-Tests`; the model (including the new status classes) is in `ISW1-2024-1C-Parcial`, and all classes have real comments now.
